stories.title: UN warns of 'supersized' El Niño as countries prepare for impact
stories.body: The WMO has warned that the natural weather phenomenon could bring disruption to global economies.

stories.title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as 'super' El Niño intensifies
stories.body: Millions of people have been exposed to the smog, with more than 12,000 children suffering respiratory issues.

stories.title: Feminist activist and journalist Gloria Steinem dies, aged 92
stories.body: Her foundation said she "passed away peacefully" at her home in New York City, "surrounded by many who loved her".

stories.title: Palestinian teens killed during settler attack on West Bank village, officials say
stories.body: Al-Mughayyir's council says they were trying to stop settlers stealing sheep, but the Israeli military says they threw stones at its troops.

stories.title: 'Beautiful, vibrant' Disney star Carla Jeffery dies aged 33
stories.body: Jeffery was known for playing cheerleader Bree in 2018 Disney Channel movie Zombies and two sequels.

stories.title: ICE agent charged with lying about shooting Venezuelan man during crackdown
stories.body: The ICE officer faces federal charges related to the January shooting in Minnesota.

stories.title: More than 80 migrants feared dead after boat rescued off Canary Islands
stories.body: Rescuers found 44 survivors on board the vessel but bad weather meant they had to leave five bodies behind.

stories.title: Anthony Joshua's driver attempted overtake before fatal crash, trial hears
stories.body: Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode is charged in Nigeria with offences including causing death by dangerous driving.

stories.title: Embattled Spanish PM insists there were no prior warnings before Ceuta crisis
stories.body: Pedro Sánchez tells parliament it is absurd to think the government knew and did nothing, after thousands join protests in Spanish cities.

stories.title: Trump $1 coin makes him first living president on US currency in a century
stories.body: The US Mint special edition is stamped with a portrait of Trump alongside the words "LIBERTY" and "IN GOD WE TRUST"

stories.title: Vance's Antichrist comments are a 'common belief', his friend tells BBC
stories.body: The US vice-president recently mused with a Christian podcast host on whether the end of the world was nigh.

stories.title: Kenyan president orders crackdown on foreigners operating small businesses
stories.body: It comes amid concerns over the growing number of traders from neighbouring countries.

stories.title: Sydney police investigate second possible mistaken identity killing in two days
stories.body: Wednesday's fatal shooting of a man in his 40s comes after a university student was gunned down on Tuesday.

stories.title: Rocky Horror star Tim Curry's cause of death revealed as coronary artery disease
stories.body: The British actor had significant conditions, cited on his death certificate in Los Angeles County.

stories.title: EU and Nato vow to step up pressure on Russia after 'new escalation' in Germany
stories.body: Russia is accused of growing increasingly reckless after Berlin blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport.

stories.title: How Gloria Steinem changed the lives of generations of women
stories.body: The trailblazing feminist spoke out for the legalisation of abortion, same-sex marriage and equal pay for women - but her activism was not without backlash.

stories.title: AI data centres are booming in Australia - but at what cost?
stories.body: Advocates say data centres will bring jobs but others worry they will suck up resources while providing little advantage.

stories.title: Why Nepal floods should worry India
stories.body: The disaster comes as a warning as climate change raises shared Himalayan risks.

stories.title: 'The crowd shouted that we'd stolen someone's genitals' - deadly rumours spread on social media
stories.body: More than 80 people have been killed in the mob violence, the BBC finds after gathering data from six African nations.

stories.title: Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice in South Africa
stories.body: At least 69 people were shot dead in 1960 but no-one has been prosecuted and victims want restitution.
